prediction:
**THIS ARM MUST RUN THE OPENGL RENDERER. `--env HAKUX_RENDERER=OPENGL`, on the
desktop channel. A HANDHELD ARM CANNOT JUDGE IT AND MUST NOT BE SPENT ON IT.**

That sentence is the whole reason this file exists. It supersedes
2026-09-20-gl-stale-surface-blit.json, which carried the same fix, the same
refs and the same numbers, and was judged FAIL by [job.arms] on a pair whose
269 captures came back BYTE-IDENTICAL between the arms. The fix is confined to
hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/gl/texture.c -- the OpenGL renderer -- and
desktop_channel.sh:627 and affinity.py:61 both say in the tree that OPENGL is
"the renderer neither handheld can run". So that arm could not have moved a
pixel whatever the code did, and byte-identity is the expected result of
running it, not evidence about the change. THE FAIL WAS MINE: the superseded
file quoted desktop-GL numbers and never said which renderer produced them,
so the outlet had nothing to route on and spent a device arm.

affinity.py's own comment describes this failure shape one door away -- a pair
sent "to a renderer nobody asked for" where "the result looks entirely
healthy". Here it looked entirely dead instead, which is luckier.

WHAT THE FIX IS. TextureBinding::data_hash describes the GUEST BYTES a binding
was generated from, and pgraph_gl_render_surface_to_texture() overwrites the
binding's pixels without touching it. The slow path then asks the hash whether
the binding matches VRAM, gets a confident wrong answer when it does, and
serves the blitted pixels as the texture the guest asked for. Fixed by
regenerating any binding with a nonzero draw_time that is wanted as a VRAM
texture; draw_time is the discriminator because generate_texture() sets it to 0
and the s2t branch is its only writer.

Instrumented at the bind on Blend_surface::DstAlpha_XA_O1A7RGB8's first
swatch: recorded data_hash 141e1a7bae3fe174, live VRAM hash 141e1a7bae3fe174
-- genuinely equal -- vram[0] 00000000, glGetTexImage[0] ffffff22 (an earlier
A8R8G8B8 blit), binding->draw_time 306824 where every other X1A7 swatch reads
0.

PREDICTED, on the OpenGL renderer, disc iso_surf1, 236 captures:

  Blend_surface/DstAlpha_XA_O1A7RGB8   90,112 -> 81,920
  the other nine A7 captures            unchanged
  ten A7 captures, GL total            458,042 -> 449,850
  those ten, GL vs Vulkan              16,384 px -> 0
  whole disc                           exactly 1 better, 0 worse, 235 same

81,920 is not a modelled number, it is VULKAN'S CURRENT VALUE on that capture:
the claim is that GL stops serving a stale blit and therefore agrees with a
renderer that never did.

ALREADY REPRODUCED FIVE TIMES ON THIS HOST, deterministically and in both
directions, which is why the arm's byte-identity is diagnosed rather than
believed: 90,112 on two runs without the fix (one of them a binary the build
had not picked up, which is itself the control) and 81,920 on three runs with
it, including one from a fresh clean build after the arm's verdict landed. The
mover is one capture and exactly one 128x64 swatch half.

FAILS IF, on an OPENGL arm: DstAlpha_XA_O1A7RGB8 is anything but 81,920; any
of the other nine A7 captures moves; or any capture on the disc gets worse.
Surface_pitch::Swizzle is EXCLUDED in both directions -- two runs of one
unchanged binary on this host read 12,224 and 11,132, so it is 1,092 px of
noise (the #39/#87 race).

A VULKAN ARM IS NOT A FAILING RESULT AND MUST NOT BE RECORDED AS ONE. If one
is run anyway, its correct verdict is "not applicable, wrong renderer", and
byte-identity between its arms CONFIRMS the change is GL-only rather than
refuting it. must_not_move is deliberately not set over the disc: the defect
is general -- any cache key shared between a surface-to-texture test and a
VRAM-texture test can hit it -- so another capture may legitimately improve,
and an improvement must be named with its capture and its delta.

THE UNCOMFORTABLE OUTCOME, named in advance. If an OpenGL arm also comes back
byte-identical, then this host's five runs are measuring something about this
container rather than about the code, and the fix is unsupported no matter how
clean those runs looked.
